documents.title: Master Direction (Synthetic) on Cyber Resilience for Digital Payment Entities

clauses.text: This direction consolidates supervisory expectations on cyber resilience for regulated digital payment entities.
It applies to payment aggregators, prepaid payment instrument issuers and their technology service providers.
Regulated entities shall report every cyber security incident affecting payment systems to the Reserve Bank within six hours of detection.
Regulated entities shall enforce multi-factor authentication for all privileged and administrative access to production systems.
Regulated entities shall conduct vulnerability assessment and penetration testing of all internet-facing applications at least quarterly.
System and security logs shall be retained for a minimum period of 180 days and shall be stored within India.
The board shall approve a cyber crisis management plan, and the plan shall be reviewed at least annually.
Regulated entities shall complete a security risk assessment of every technology vendor before onboarding.
Regulated entities should conduct periodic cyber drills involving senior management and key technology staff.

documents.title: Personal Data Breach and Consent Rules (Synthetic Guidance)

clauses.text: These rules supplement the general obligations of data fiduciaries that process digital personal data.
A data fiduciary shall maintain verifiable records of consent obtained from each data principal, including the purpose and timestamp of consent.
In the event of a personal data breach, the data fiduciary shall notify each affected data principal without undue delay and in any case within 72 hours.
Personal data shall be erased once the specified purpose is served, unless retention is required by law.
Before processing the personal data of a child, the data fiduciary shall obtain verifiable consent of the parent or lawful guardian.
The data fiduciary shall publish the business contact information of its Data Protection Officer on its website and mobile application.

documents.title: Outsourcing of IT Services - Amendment Circular (Synthetic)

clauses.text: Regulated entities shall assess concentration risk arising from dependence on a single cloud or IT service provider at least annually.
Regulated entities shall maintain a documented and tested exit strategy for every critical IT service provider.
Every outsourcing agreement shall include a clause granting the regulated entity and the Reserve Bank the right to audit the service provider.
Regulated entities may establish an independent technology risk committee at the board level to oversee outsourcing arrangements.
